title: Finding the nearest 24/7 vet ED
why_this_matters: The nearest open veterinary ER may not be the nearest clinic, and deciding where to go before an emergency saves time; the app supports two ways to find one (this is product guidance, not a clinical claim, and needs reviewer sign-off).

what_changes_from_human.point: There is no national dispatch that routes a dog to an open veterinary ER the way 911 routes a person, so the handler must know or find the clinic.

recognition: Local missions: record the 24/7 emergency vets for each area you work on the K9 profile (Vet ER screen, or K9 profiles then Edit), and note which accept working dogs.
Unfamiliar territory: use the Vet ER screen's search, which opens your phone's maps app. The app does not read your location or look anything up itself.
management: Call before you drive. Opening hours shown in maps or saved earlier can be wrong, so confirm they are open and can see your dog.
Saved entries show when they were last verified and flag any older than 180 days (a product default); re-verify by phone and update the date.
Directions are offered only for saved clinics that have an address, so a name alone cannot send you to the wrong town.
Hand over with the Handoff summary so the receiving clinic gets the dog's weight (and whether estimated), MDR1 status and what was done.

takeaway: Know where you would go before you need to: save 24/7 ERs for the work area, and in a new area search in maps and call ahead.
